message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.21","text":"When he had said these things, I answered, “Already I give thanks to God, for just as I wished to be fully assured, so he has granted it to me. Nevertheless, be utterly unconcerned about me: I will never doubt—so much so that, even if you yourself should ever wish to move me away from the prophetic thesis, you would be powerless and unable to do so. So well do I know what I have received. And do not suppose that in saying this—that I will never doubt—I am making you some great promise. Rather, neither I myself nor any other human being who has listened to the discourse about a prophet will ever be able to doubt the true thesis, after first hearing and understanding what the truth of prophetic proclamation is. Therefore, be confident in the teaching willed by God, for every craft of evil has been defeated. Against prophecy nothing has any power: neither verbal arts nor contrivances of sophisms, neither syllogisms nor any other device—provided, at least, that the one who has listened to a true prophet genuinely desires truth and is not, under the pretext of truth, looking around for something else. So, my lord Peter, do not lose heart as though you had bestowed the greatest good on someone without perception. For you bestowed it on one who perceives the favor and cannot be led astray from the truth that was given. For I know that there are things a person wants both to receive quickly and not to obtain slowly. Therefore I know not to despise, because it came quickly, the incomparable and only secure thing given to me.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὡς γὰρ ἐβουλόμην πληροφορηθῆναι","chosen":"just as I wished to be fully assured","rationale":"The passive πληροφορηθῆναι denotes attaining full assurance rather than merely receiving information."},{"source_quote":"τῆς προφητικῆς ὑποθέσεως","chosen":"the prophetic thesis","rationale":"Ὑπόθεσις here denotes the position or foundational proposition concerning prophecy; “thesis” preserves that conceptual sense."},{"source_quote":"προφητικῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἀλήθεια","chosen":"the truth of prophetic proclamation","rationale":"In this discussion of prophetic authority, ἐπαγγελία is treated as a proclamation or claim rather than necessarily a promise about the future."},{"source_quote":"τῷ θεοβουλήτῳ δόγματι","chosen":"the teaching willed by God","rationale":"This renders the compound θεοβούλητος explicitly while taking δόγμα as an authoritative teaching."},{"source_quote":"οὔτε τέχναι λόγων οὔτε σοφισμάτων ἐπίνοιαι, οὐ συλλογισμοί, οὐκ ἄλλη τις μηχανή","chosen":"neither verbal arts nor contrivances of sophisms, neither syllogisms nor any other device","rationale":"The rendering preserves the ordered list of rhetorical arts, invented sophisms, formal arguments, and other mechanisms."},{"source_quote":"οὐ προφάσει ἀληθείας ἕτερόν τι περιβλέπεται","chosen":"is not, under the pretext of truth, looking around for something else","rationale":"Περιβλέπεται retains the image of looking about for another objective while using truth as a pretext."},{"source_quote":"μὴ ἀθύμει ὡς ἀναισθήτῳ τὸ μέγιστον δωρησάμενος ἀγαθόν· αἰσθομένῳ γὰρ χάριτος ἐδωρήσω","chosen":"do not lose heart as though you had bestowed the greatest good on someone without perception. For you bestowed it on one who perceives the favor","rationale":"“Without perception” and “perceives” preserve the contrast between ἀναίσθητος and αἰσθάνομαι."},{"source_quote":"ἀπατηθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δοθέντος ἀληθοῦς","chosen":"be led astray from the truth that was given","rationale":"The neuter substantive ἀληθές is rendered “truth,” while ἀπό is taken with a separative force."},{"source_quote":"ἔνεστιν ὧν βούλεταί τις καὶ ταχέως λαβεῖν καὶ βραδέως μὴ τυχεῖν","chosen":"there are things a person wants both to receive quickly and not to obtain slowly","rationale":"Βούλεται governs both coordinated infinitival expressions, preserving the pointed contrast between quick and delayed acquisition."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ δοθέντος μοι διὰ τὸ τάχος ἀσυγκρίτου καὶ μόνου ἀσφαλοῦς","chosen":"because it came quickly, the incomparable and only secure thing given to me","rationale":"The genitive adjectives describe what was given, while διὰ τὸ τάχος explains the possible ground for undervaluing it."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.22","text":"After I had said these things, Peter said, “I acknowledge my gratitude to God both for your salvation and for my own delight. For I truly rejoice, knowing that you have recognized just what the greatness of prophecy is. Since, then, as you said, even if I myself should ever wish—may that never happen!—to move you over to another teaching, I would be unable to persuade you, begin from tomorrow onward to be present with me at the debates with the opponents. My debate tomorrow is with Simon the magician.” After saying this and himself partaking of food, he instructed me too to partake separately. Then, after offering a blessing over the food and giving thanks, when he had eaten his fill and had also given me the explanation of this very matter, he went on to say, “May God grant you to become like me in every respect and, once you have been baptized, to share the same table with me.” After saying this, he instructed me to rest, for by then, I suppose, the nature of the body was demanding sleep as well.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Χάριν ὁμολογῶ τῷ θεῷ","chosen":"I acknowledge my gratitude to God","rationale":"Ὁμολογῶ gives the thanksgiving the force of an expressed acknowledgment."},{"source_quote":"περὶ τῆς ἐμῆς ἀπολαύσεως","chosen":"for my own delight","rationale":"Ἀπόλαυσις denotes the enjoyment or delight Peter himself receives from Clement’s response."},{"source_quote":"ὅπερ ἀπείη","chosen":"may that never happen!","rationale":"The optative expresses a strong wish that the contemplated change of teaching remain far removed."},{"source_quote":"ἄρξαι τοῦ λοιποῦ ἀπὸ τῆς αὔριον παρεῖναί μοι","chosen":"begin from tomorrow onward to be present with me","rationale":"“From tomorrow onward” represents both ἀπὸ τῆς αὔριον and the prospective force of τοῦ λοιποῦ."},{"source_quote":"ἐν ταῖς τῶν ἀντικειμένων ζητήσεσιν","chosen":"at the debates with the opponents","rationale":"Ζητήσεις denotes adversarial discussions here, and the genitive identifies the opposing participants."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς Σίμωνα μάγον","chosen":"with Simon the magician","rationale":"Μάγος is translated as a descriptive designation rather than imported in its Latinized form “Magus.”"},{"source_quote":"ἰδία κἀμὲ μεταλαβεῖν ἐκέλευσεν","chosen":"he instructed me too to partake separately","rationale":"The rendering follows the apparent intended adverbial sense, supported by the subsequent distinction between separate eating and sharing Peter’s table after baptism."},{"source_quote":"αὐτοῦ τούτου τὸν λόγον μοι ἀποδοὺς","chosen":"having also given me the explanation of this very matter","rationale":"Τὸν λόγον ἀποδιδόναι here means supplying an account or explanation."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ πάντα ἐξομοιωθῆναί μοι","chosen":"to become like me in every respect","rationale":"The passive ἐξομοιωθῆναι expresses being brought into full likeness, with κατὰ πάντα specifying every respect."},{"source_quote":"βαπτισθέντα τῆς αὐτῆς μοι μεταλαβεῖν τραπέζης","chosen":"once you have been baptized, to share the same table with me","rationale":"The participle makes baptism antecedent to participation, and μεταλαβεῖν with the genitive is naturally rendered “share.”"},{"source_quote":"ἤδη γάρ που καὶ τὸν ὕπνον ἀπῄτει ἡ τοῦ σώματος φύσις","chosen":"for by then, I suppose, the nature of the body was demanding sleep as well","rationale":"The enclitic που gives the statement a mildly tentative, inferential force."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἰδία","issue":"The supplied reading lacks the iota subscript required for the apparent dative-adverb form “separately”; as printed, it does not fit the evident adverbial syntax.","proposed_reading":"ἰδίᾳ","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
